title: Simultaneous Competitive and Regret Guarantees for TCP Acknowledgment
abstract: arXiv:2610.13571v1 Announce Type: new  Abstract: We study simultaneous competitive and regret guarantees for TCP acknowledgment. Each acknowledgment serves all pending packets, and the objective is to minimize the total acknowledgment and waiting costs. It is well known that no deterministic online algorithm achieves a competitive ratio better than $2$. Given $k$ randomized online experts and $0<\varepsilon<1$, we construct a randomized online algorithm whose realized total cost is always at most $(2+\varepsilon)$ times the offline optimal cost $\mathrm{OPT}$ and whose expected regret against the expert with the smallest realized cost is $O(\sqrt{\mathrm{OPT}\log(k+1)}+\log(1/\varepsilon))$. The algorithm requires no advance knowledge of the number of packets or $\mathrm{OPT}$. Our algorithm controls switching costs between experts and uses the gap between the permitted competitive bound and its current cost to determine when to learn. tldr: 该论文为TCP确认问题提出了一种随机化在线算法，在无需预先知道报文数量或离线最优成本的情况下，同时实现了(2+ε)的竞争比保证和相对于最优专家的次线性期望遗憾。
en_tdlr: The paper proposes a randomized online algorithm for TCP acknowledgment that simultaneously achieves a (2+ε)-competitive ratio and sublinear expected regret against the best expert, without any prior knowledge of the number of packets or the offline optimum.
